newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes slightly down vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes slightly down vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly down against the dollar on Thursday on late demand for the U.S. currency for import covering, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 57.65 to the dollar and traded in a narrow range for much of the day before closing at 57.68. It closed at 57.73 on Wednesday.
"Being the month end, people are not prepared to create new positions, minus or plus. So the market is not very active," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by quarter local cent, fixing buying and selling rates at 56.6107 and 57.7543.
Overnight call money, which opened at 12.75, shot up to 17 percent before settling down to close at 13.5 percent.
"There were some big borrowers in the market today," said a Hatton National Bank dealer. "Money went up because banks were forced to borrow to meet their reserve with the Central Bank."
